subject: Post-call: Aurora Health inference discovery — latency, throughput & geo constraints
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Aurora Health inference discovery — latency, throughput & geo constraints

Hi Aditi (and team),

Thanks again for the call today — useful discussion. Wanted to capture the requirements we heard and outline next steps so we're all aligned. Please correct anything inaccurate.

Summary (what Aurora told us)
- Primary workload: interactive patient triage chat + episodic summarization. Latency & streaming are critical for the chat flow.
- P95 latency target (interactive): ~150 ms for short, single-turn prompts (< 80 tokens response).
- Streaming requirement: first-token RTT target <= 80 ms from request acceptance for real-time UX; subsequent tokens streaming at ~10-20 ms/token is desirable.
- Throughput & concurrency: steady-state 500 QPS globally with burst capacity to ~3,000 QPS for 60-90s spikes; expected concurrency ~400 concurrent sessions (avg), peaks ~1,200.
- Payloads: avg prompt = 350 tokens (including context), avg response = 80 tokens. Some flows will send 2–3 sequential calls per session.
- Regional expectations: 70% traffic from US, 20% EU, 10% APAC. EU traffic must remain in-region for processing (data residency requirement). APAC can be routed to SG or US as long as latency stays within bounds and data residency for APAC customers is documented.
- Security/compliance: Aurora requires SOC 2 reports and DPA language; legal contact is cc'd and will share a DPA template.

Open questions / items we need from Aurora
- Confirm the exact PII classification and any fields that must be redacted before leaving customer network.
- Provide representative sample payloads (x3: small, medium, large) and expected token counts.
- Expected daily throughput profile (CSV preferred) — you mentioned a weekly rhythm; please share the CSV we can use for load modeling.
- Any hard requirement that EU requests cannot transit or be processed in the US (we heard "must stay in EU" but want explicit confirmation).

Redwood initial read (quick feasibility notes)
- We can meet the first-token streaming target in US and EU with a dedicated regional pool + lightweight batching. APAC will require either a local SG pool or an optimized cross-region fallback to keep latency low.
- For the EU data residency ask, two practical options: (1) Dedicated EU-only deployment (private/dedicated) where all inference instances live in EU region; or (2) Hosted routing with guaranteed EU-only model instances and contractual residency guarantees. We'll outline tradeoffs in the follow-up doc.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Aurora: share sample payloads and the CSV traffic profile (attachment: aurora_traffic_estimate.csv).
2) Redwood: prepare a technical options doc + cost delta for dedicated EU pool vs hosted EU-only routing.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with SREs (90 min) to validate concurrency/streaming, ideally next week — propose Tue/Wed.
4) Aurora legal: share DPA / any residency-specific clauses you need.

Attachments: aurora_traffic_estimate.csv (sample traffic profile), call recording link included below.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internal next steps and loop in our solutions SREs.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the write-up, looks right to me. A couple clarifications and numbers from our side: 

- P95 latency: yes, target 150 ms for short answers (<= 80 tokens); we can tolerate up to 250 ms for longer generations but want to flag UX regressions over 200 ms.
- Streaming: first token < 80 ms is a hard requirement for the main triage chat. Subsequent tokens can stream with a <25ms/token cadence.
- Throughput: baseline 500 QPS with scheduled daily peaks (we’ll attach the CSV). Bursts: up to 3k QPS for 1–2 minutes during event-driven spikes.
- Concurrency: global active sessions ~400 average, peaks 1.2k. Per-region concurrency expectation: US peak ~900, EU peak ~220, APAC peak ~80.
- Data residency: EU user data cannot be routed or processed outside the EU. That includes model context/state and KV cache. APAC users: prefer in-region processing (SG) but can accept SG->US fallback for resilience if explicitly documented.
- Models: we plan to evaluate a 8B dense open model (quantized) initially; may test a 13B variant for higher quality.

Attachments: I’m attaching the traffic CSV and a preliminary SLO matrix (aurora_slo_matrix.xlsx). Legal will follow with DPA/clauses by EOD tomorrow.

Happy to jump on the SRE deep-dive — Tue 26 Apr 10:00 PT works for us.

— Aditi
Aditi Shah
Head of Product, Aurora Health

Quick internal assessment and asks before the SRE deep-dive: 

Short summary: feasible with a mix of dedicated regional capacity + routing controls. EU residency will drive either dedicated EU pool or private deployment.

Technical notes:
- First-token latency: achievable in US/EU with aggressive connection warm pools + no-batch for low-latency paths. For streaming-first-token <80ms we recommend a small always-warm fleet per region (min 3 instances) with autoscale headroom for bursts.
- Throughput/bursting: continuous batching + adaptive batching policies will reduce token cost, but we must cap batch latency for chat flows. We can hit 3k QPS bursts using a combination of warm VMs and ephemeral burst workers; need to size GPU counts based on sample payloads.
- Persistence & KV: to honor EU residency, KV caches and prefix caches must be region-isolated — cannot sync back to US. That will increase cost for EU.
- Model variants: 8B quantized will likely meet latency; 13B requires more headroom and will push cost up ~1.8–2x for same SLOs.

Action items for the deep-dive (Ben/Karthik to lead):
1) Aurora to share sample payloads and CSV traffic (they sent these, thanks) — we’ll use them to run a quick load model.
2) Redwood to prepare three deployment options doc (attached: proposed_deployment_options.pdf): hosted multi-geo with EU-only routing, dedicated EU pool, and private EU deployment (on-prem/VPC) with quick cost delta.
3) Bring infra SRE (Evelyn) + runtime lead (Karthik) + solutions engineer (Ben) to the call. We’ll validate warm pool sizes and produce a preliminary capacity estimate.
4) Legal/Procurement: Tessa to attach DPA/contract ask to the HubSpot deal (deal AH-2026-09).

I’ll prep rough GPU counts after we profile the sample payloads.

— Ben
